lines: A quiet night where the steam from the bath melted into the moon.
The air was so clear it seemed to filter even the starlight, allowing a clear view of the vibrant autumn foliage, with red and yellow hues intermingling in the darkness.
The onset of winter had colored the maples and lulled the insects to sleep. The chill of the night air was soothed by the medicinal bath, caressing the skin with the pleasant warmth of late autumn.
I rested my arms on the edge of the tub and sank into the medicinal bath, letting the comfort of the water rising slowly from my feet soak in the entirety of the day.
Me
The heat seeped into my body. I exhaled the fatigue that had been driven out by the resonating comfort as a soundless breath.
First to the night air, then to the heat, my tense body began to unravel and loosen, much like the rising steam that dissolved into the air.
When I turned my gaze, I saw Dutch was also quietly submerged in the water.
The steady movement of his thick chest made it clear he was relaxed.
Leaning his muscular frame against the edge of the tub, I could tell Dutch was also dissolving the day into the medicinal bath.
A gust of wind blew through. The steam was pushed aside, and a yellow leaf detached from a branch, fluttering down to the surface of the water.
Dutch
Seeing that, Dutch let out a small sigh.
It was a candid exhalation, as if he were releasing the comfort that had soaked into his body directly outward.
I stared at the falling leaf and spoke.
Me
I'm sorry. I should have explained beforehand.
Me
Being in a state of near-nudity with someone in an outdoor bath is... not something that normally happens.
While it is a cultural thing, for me, surrounded by allies in a country with high public safety like Japan, it is not that much of a departure from the everyday.
However, from Dutch's perspective, it is a culture he is unfamiliar with to begin with, and he is right in the middle of people whose allegiance wavers between enemy and ally.
Dutch
I was just a bit taken aback. Whether it was the location or the facilities, I could see the security was tight.
Dutch
I found it crazy and amusing that you could so casually pull off the act of not caring if you got killed at any moment.
Me
Hahaha...
The open-air bath may look defenseless at first glance, but surveillance and security are thorough in the surrounding area.
If something were to happen and we had to fight, the security personnel would surely move before we did.
Dutch
Besides. ...I can't tell just by looking from here, but the surveillance and security are thorough, right?
Me
Yes, that is certainly the case.
It was a statement of trust in us. I nodded in return, accepting it as such.
Dutch
Since I said I "understood," I can't just trample on the Japanese concept of "omotenashi" hospitality.
Dutch
I'll enjoy myself.
Dutch shrugged lightly and let a smile play on his lips.
To savor, to relax. Even if one feels resistance, one accepts it, entrusts oneself to it, and asserts one's will.
It is not about becoming familiar or complacent, nor is it about yielding oneself.
Without a word, through one's demeanor, every single utterance, and even the slightest gesture, one's solid existence is made manifest.
I was made to think of him as an intelligent person who should not be taken lightly, and I was impressed.
Dutch
...I've been saying this and that, but this medicinal bath, this outdoor hot spring, isn't bad once you get in.
The open sky with no ceiling, the moon and the autumn leaves, the scent of the steam. Dutch murmured toward the silence of the night that enveloped it all.
Dutch
It makes sense that the stench of those cursed objects, which looked like shit, would disappear if you soak in this.
Dutch
It's a real sensation, you know.
Me
Did he truly like it? I exhaled slowly before opening my mouth in response to Dutch's words.
Me
...Hot springs have long been believed to possess various therapeutic effects and have become deeply rooted in our culture.
Me
In fact, past Taimanin knew that they had effects beyond what is generally said, and they utilized them in their battles against demons.
My body, which felt like it was dissolving into the water, and my mind, which was soothed by the crisp air at the border of autumn and winter.
In the sense of self-forgetfulness unique to open-air baths, the knowledge I had gained from reading materials in the library flowed out as if spilling over.
Me
A lost arm grew back... eyes that could not see began to see... the poison of death was drawn from the body...
Me
We have not found any hot spring with such potent effects...
Me
Was it lost? Did something change with the passage of time? Or was it never there to begin with?
Me
The advancement of medicine, the development of science, the spread of demonic technology.
Me
With the progress of technology, hot springs with weak effects faded away as a medical treatment, but...
Me
Someone revisited them, researched them anew, and found effective ways to use them... I hear they are gradually yielding results.
I poured the scooped water over my shoulders, which had been exposed to the outside air. My skin was cool from the exposure, and the warm medicinal bath felt pleasant.
The trees rustled in the wind. The sound soaked into the steam, and my mind felt as if it were being washed clean.
Me
Ah, that's right. The fact that it is outdoors...
Me

The scenery of the open-air bath, and the balance between body temperature and outside air, bring about a state of concentration and self-forgetfulness similar to meditation, which is said to enhance the medicinal effects.
The talk about meditation was only half true.
But as I soaked my body and gazed at the scenery, my consciousness dissolved, and I fell into a strange sensation where my thoughts became sharp.
Just being in an open-air bath would not produce this effect. It is certainly the medicinal bath that gives it a boost.
Dutch
Dutch looked the same way. He was not ignoring me, nor was he not listening.
He was probably just watching the ice in his glass melt, simply observing this moment.
Dutch
...If a request came in to transport a Japanese bath, I might be able to refrain from laughing.
I smiled a little at Dutch's words. It sounded like a joke, but it did not seem to be one.
Dutch
I don't know if it's a cursed object, but... I can't remember today's wounds, or when they were from. Old scars are being tickled...
Dutch
Like right before a scab falls off.
Hearing that, I noticed I had a similar sensation in my body.
It wasn't itchy enough to scratch, but there was a tickling feeling. And a gentle warmth too.
Me
I feel it too...
Dutch
Huh...
Dutch let out a breath that clearly indicated he was laughing.
At his own unexpected laugh, the corner of his mouth was pulled up widely.
Dutch
No... I guess I liked it more than I expected. I actually thought about carrying you.
As if enjoying his own unexpected reaction, Dutch turned his face toward me and spoke.
Dutch
Immediately after, Dutch turned back to face the scenery.
I, too, remained in that pleasant state, gazing at the autumn leaves, the moon, the stars, the wind, and the clouds.
My thoughts were sharp, but my consciousness was melting.
From a head that had begun to melt, still retaining some coldness like ice cream turned into sherbet, words spilled out incoherently.
Dutch and I sometimes reacted to each other, and sometimes did not.
Without any sense of time, we exchanged words sporadically.
In the midst of a silence whose count I had lost, Dutch spoke up quietly.
Dutch
...I'm glad it wasn't some superhero without a cape I was dealing with.
I knew these were words spoken with clear intent.
And so, what entered my ears called the shape of "me" back into my sherbet-like head.
Me
Is that saying it's because of me...?
Dutch
Ah... when you hear that someone fights "demons" for the sake of others.
Dutch
It makes you wonder if he's a lunatic who heard a trumpet and lost his mind.
I know that even if I told someone with no connection to demons about their existence, or about the Demon Realm where they reside, they wouldn't understand.
In fact, if they accepted it too easily, I'd be the one feeling afraid.
I could only laugh in response to this.
Me
So I wasn't a superhero, were I?
However, what Dutch was talking about wasn't that shallow question of whether one existed or not.
Dutch
You and your comrades get hurt, and you hesitate. You cherish your lives, and you trample over them when necessary.
Dutch
The "demons" are the same.
Dutch
When they bleed, they howl in pain and struggle to survive.
Dutch
It means neither side hears any trumpets; we are living beings without divine protection.
My past battles came to mind.
Me
If I had been a flawless hero...
The people I fought, the people I saved, the people I couldn't save.
The people I met, and the people I can never meet again.
So many faces flash before my eyes. Their voices come back to life.
If I had been a flawless hero, and if I had caught everything that slipped through my fingers.
Me
I... still don't think that's the case...
I can't even bring myself to think how wonderful it would have been if that were true.
Me
There are feelings that crush my chest. Things that make me want to scream.
It wasn't a fear of great power. It was a chill at the simplicity of the idea that excluding someone or something would solve everything.
I feel that the pain of my torn chest cannot be resolved in such a way.
Me
That is precisely why, thinking about being such a superhero makes me feel afraid.
Dutch
Ah, a guy like that wouldn't need a courier. Business wouldn't work either.
Me
I feel the same way.
Dutch
Hmph...
Dutch raised the corner of his mouth widely at my retort.
From Dutch's perspective, the existence of demons and Taimanin must feel like a fantasy, like a picture book of superheroes and villains, justice and evil.
But from my perspective, the opposite is also true.
The underworld where Dutch and his people exist, built on and circulating through pure human desires and vices, also seemed like a fantasy world to me.
It's not that I don't know about that kind of world, but where we step into it, there are shadows of demons, and we are chasing them.
A world where there is no absolute power gap, unresistable like that of demons.
There may be differences in status, but anyone who takes a bullet to a vital spot loses their life.
With that same weight of life, we sometimes point guns at each other, and sometimes entrust our backs to one another.
Dutch
Through communication called business, weighing profits and power dynamics, and losing even one's life when defeated.
In such a world, burning desires and sharpening skills until the moment life runs out.
And yet, it's not that there is no loyalty or human sentiment. A society where the clear and the murky mix like a rushing stream.
Me
Slaying demons that threaten the human world. It certainly sounds like a superhero.
The moon trembles on the surface of the medicinal bath. A red leaf flutters down into the moon, and the reflection ripples.
Dutch
Haaah...
Suddenly, Dutch leaned his back heavily against the edge of the tub, gazed up at the sky, and let out a long breath.
It was the familiar sound of someone relaxing in a hot spring.
Dutch
...I don't need anything else, no alcohol or cigarettes. This kind of silence is precious.
His voice was absorbed by the steam, leaving only the lingering echo.
I soaked in Dutch's words and this silence for a while before nodding.
Me
...I don't understand the appeal of alcohol and cigarettes, but I do like this quietness.
Dutch answered while still looking up at the sky.
Dutch
Yeah, it really isn't bad...
After that, there were no more words. We just sank into the bath and continued to savor the silence.
